expectations.text: Rejects or substantially scales back the twelve-theme monthly calendar rather than refining, filling in, or endorsing it.
expectations.evidence: "don't run the twelve-month calendar. Post three things in October, then go quiet on purpose until spring."

expectations.text: Grounds the cadence choice in who has recurring hours in the quiet months, not in the team's current post-edition enthusiasm.
expectations.evidence: "Occasional pulse needs someone with recurring hours in the gap. Q8 says nobody has them."

expectations.text: Identifies the proposed plan (live AMAs, new sub-channels, standing prompts) as the heaviest cadence posture, which requires funded or guaranteed moderation capacity this volunteer team lacks.
expectations.evidence: "combines the two heaviest rungs... Continuous heavy needs all three... a funded moderator roster exists"

expectations.text: Recommends dormant-but-open, or at most a light occasional pulse, as the posture for this team.
expectations.evidence: "Chosen rung: dormant-but-open."

expectations.text: States that a recurring digest or spotlight rhythm is only viable when one named person holds recurring hours across the whole gap, and lapses otherwise.
expectations.evidence: "Optional, only if one person volunteers and can hold it... If it lapses, record the missed month."

expectations.text: Names, or requires the team to name, a single owner for the chosen posture, and states that a cadence with no named owner is not a decided posture.
expectations.evidence: Requires a named owner, but says "If nobody will put their name on it, the posture is dormant by decision", not that it is undecided.

expectations.text: Warns that a published calendar the team then abandons reads worse to members than deliberate, stated silence.
expectations.evidence: "It is abandoned by the fourth slot, and the abandonment is more visible than the silence."

expectations.text: If dormancy is chosen, prescribes one pinned dated notice containing a date tied to the next build-up, a named owner, a conduct-report route that still works, and a promise small enough to keep.
expectations.evidence: "It needs four things: a date, a named owner, a conduct route that works, and a promise small enough to keep."

expectations.text: States that dormancy keeps the archive readable and the member list intact and owned; it is not deleting or closing the server.
expectations.evidence: "Close the server and reopen fresh | ❌ Never | Discards the member list and archive"

expectations.text: Any pulse plan proposed fills its slots from material that already exists (edition recordings, members' own posts) rather than requiring original content per slot.
expectations.evidence: "Source material must already exist. Skip this if it needs original work."

expectations.text: Treats missed posting cycles as a signal to demote the cadence next gap, not as a team-discipline problem to push through.
expectations.evidence: "Two missed cycles means demote, and that is a signal, not a discipline problem."

expectations.text: Requires the member list to have a named owner and a written retention decision at the start of the gap, whatever cadence is chosen.
expectations.evidence: "List integrity (gate) | Owner and written retention decision exist | By the day the gap starts"

expectations.text: Does not set message-volume, engagement-rate, or activity targets for the space as success measures.
expectations.evidence: "The count of messages, members or reactions is not a measure here."
